conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Lichtenberg
style.description: Fractal wood burning: a pale maple board on a dark slate workbench mat with two copper electrodes clamped to it. A high-voltage discharge burns a branching Lichtenberg figure into the wood between them. The whole tree is planned once, seeded (space colonisation from the first electrode, half-width from downstream length, a burn time per node, dead ends everywhere and exactly one path that reaches the second electrode) and baked into a distance + burn-time field; at time t each groove is drawn up to its burn front: white-blue arc at the tip, glowing orange ember just behind, near-black char with a soft brown scorch halo after. When the one path connects, a return stroke flashes back along it, the channel widens and stays glowing. Smoke wisps, flickering tip glints, the crackle, the hum and the connection crack all come from the same plan.

map.description: dark slate cutting mat with a faint 5 cm grid

motion: Nothing is simulated per frame: the tree, its widths and every node's burn time are planned once; a groove at time t is drawn up to (t - ta) / (tb - ta).

Three ages of a burn: white-blue arc at the front (under 0.1 s), orange ember cooling to dark red behind it (about half a second, longer on thick trunks), then black char with a brown scorch halo that keeps spreading for a second.
Side branches slow down as they die; the winning path keeps a steady crawl, then leaps the last gap.
The connection: a return stroke runs back along the winning path in a quarter second, the room light dips, the channel widens and stays glowing.
Camera: one rise from a low three-quarter view to near top-down while the tree spreads, then locked; a few millimetres of shake on the connection.

notes.mechanism: burnplan.js: seeded space-colonisation tree from the question electrode (one branch reaches the answer electrode), half-width from downstream length, a burn time per node (winning path: steady crawl + leap at `connect`; side branches slow down and die before it). Baked once into a distance + burn-time field; the board shader draws arc / ember / char / scorch / return stroke from one time uniform.
notes.honesty: A picture of the idea, not of the mechanism: a real model does not burn paths; the tree stands for many candidate continuations being weighed and one being kept.
